description: The bar chart illustrates the difference in average Word Error Rate (WER) from the Whisper baseline model when various text preprocessing optimizations are applied, comparing performance between two fine-tuned models: NESAC ft model (orange bars) and SESHA ft model (green bars). The vertical axis lists five optimization categories — “Normalised,” “Add Spacing,” “Remove Spacing,” “Americanisms,” and “Dates” — arranged from top to bottom in descending order of WER difference for the NESAC model. The horizontal axis represents the “Difference in Average WER from Whisper,” scaled from 0.000 to 0.003 in increments of 0.001. For each optimization, two adjacent horizontal bars show the WER delta for each model, with numerical values labeled at the end of each bar. The NESAC model consistently exhibits higher WER differences than SESHA across all optimizations, with the largest difference observed under “Normalised” (0.00323 for NESAC vs. 0.00313 for SESHA), and the smallest under “Dates” (0.00257 for NESAC vs. 0.00228 for SESHA). The chart visually emphasizes that applying these text normalizations generally degrades performance relative to the Whisper baseline, with “Normalised” having the most negative impact and “Dates” the least. The models are distinguished by color in a legend at the bottom right, with orange for NESAC and green for SESHA.
